summary: The root حظظ primarily means to have good fortune, luck, or a portion allotted by fate.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: حَظَّ حظ, sec. pers. حَظِظْتَ, (S, K,) aor. يَحَظُّ, (S,) inf. n. حَظٌّ, (K,) He was, or became, fortunate, or possessed of good fortune, (S, K,) فِى الأَمْرِ in the affair; (K;) as also: (K, TA:) or ↓ the latter signifies he was, or became, rich, wealthy, or opulent; or in a state of, or possessed of, competence, or sufficiency; in no need; without wants; or with few wants.

أَحْظَظَ see 1, in two places. أَحْظَيْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ [ I preferred him above him ] may be from the same root as the other words of this art.; the second ظ being changed into ى; [like as أَمْلَيْتُ is, accord. to some, formed from أَمْلَلْتُ;] or it may be from حُظْوَةٌ. (TA.)

حَظٌّ حظ Fortune; or particularly good fortune; syn. جَدٌّ (S, Nh, Msb, K) and بَخْتٌ: (Nh:) and a share, portion, or lot: (S, Msb, K:) or particularly a share, portion, or lot, of something good or excellent: (Lth, K:) some of the people of Hims say حَنْزٌ; but when they form a pl., they return to the original, saying حُظُوظٌ: and the ن is regarded by them as a nasal sound, not as a radical letter: and in like manner they do in the case of every word having a doubled letter, such as رُزٌّ and…
حِظَآءٌ حظآء and حِظَّآءٌ: see حَظٌّ.
حَظِّىٌّ حظ حظى حظي حظيي, or حَظِىٌّ: see what next follows.

حَظِيظٌ حظيظ and (S, K) and, as a relative n., accord. to [most of] the copies of the K, or as a defective word, [i. e., with a single ظ, as we find it in the CK,] accord. to Az, who says that it is originally حَظٌّ, (TA,) and, (AA, S, Msb, K,) Fortunate; or possessed of good fortune; (S, Msb, K;) possessing a good share ( حَظٌّ ) of the means of subsistence: (TA:) or the first, accord. to Fr, possessing competence, or sufficiency; or rich, or wealthy, or opulent: (TA:) the pl. [accord.
فُلَانٌ أَحَظُّ مِنْ فُلَانٍ Such a one is more fortunate than such a one. (S, * Msb, * TA.)
أَحَاظٍ said to be an irreg. pl. of حَظٌّ, q. v.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
